newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Africa lobbies S.E.Asia on sagging coffee prices.
newsitem.headline: Africa lobbies S.E.Asia on sagging coffee prices.

text.p: African coffee producers are lobbying Indonesia and Vietnam to rein in exports to boost sagging world prices, officials said on Tuesday.

The African moves come ahead of an emergency meeting of coffee producers in Brazil next week to discuss a proposal by the InterAfrican Coffee Organisation (IACO) to trim exports by up to 2.5 million 60-kilogram bags in the first half of 1997.
The IACO is also appealing to Vietnam, the second biggest coffee producer in Asia after Indonesia, to join the 14-member Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC).

"We have a message to the president of Vietnam trying to see if they can join the ACPC," Ugandan Minister of State for Trade and Industry Abel Rwendeire told Reuters in an interview at the Asia Coffee conference in Ho Chi Minh City.
Vietnam has previously resisted joining the ACPC.
"The Vietnamese just don't see any benefit in going into the ACPC," a coffee trader attending the conference said.

Rwendeire said the African states were also trying to overcome Indonesian objections to joining the retention plan. "What does it profit you to push 1,000 tonnes and you get the price for only 500 tonnes?" he asked.
Rwendeire said he was confident that Indonesia will come around to supporting the retention scheme to hold back up to 2.5 million bags from the market in an attempt to lift prices.
Indonesia, a member of the ACPC, has said it would be pointless to implement an export reduction plan if Vietnam stayed out of the association and sold coffee without restrictions.
In mid-December, Paian Nainggolan, Indonesia's government representative to the ACPC, told Reuters Jakarta would not back the African efforts to bolster prices by cutting exports.
"If we restrain our supplies, there are free riders in the region who will take our market," he said.
An Indonesian delegate at the conference in Ho Chi Minh City said: "It would be hard for us to come on board."

The chairman of the IACO, Ivory Coast commodities minister Guy-Alain Gauze, and the organization's chief economist, Donald Kaberuka, were due in Ho Chi Minh City on Tuesday and were expected to fly to Hanoi later in the week to present a letter from African coffee producers to Vietnam's government.
